subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trusted host-read HTML lifecycle for outbound-staged generated reports?
rationale: The patch fixes a real Telegram message-loss regression, but it deliberately extends a local HTML host-read security boundary beyond the temp root; automation cannot decide that trust policy for maintainers.

options.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
options.body: After rebase, land this design with security/owner signoff because trust is bound to the staged bytes, source provenance, and fail-closed DB checks.

options.title: Require A Narrower Lifecycle
options.body: Ask for a revised design if maintainers want a different marker owner, retention policy, or non-persistent trust model before expanding the boundary.

options.title: Keep Staged HTML Blocked
options.body: Reject the trust expansion and leave generated HTML delivery fail-closed after staging, accepting the current Telegram regression until another design exists.

recommendation.title: Accept Content-Bound Provenance
recommendation.body: After rebase, land this design with security/owner signoff because trust is bound to the staged bytes, source provenance, and fail-closed DB checks.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the trusted generated HTML host-read behavior that defines the boundary this PR extends.
